reasons: Correct classification: Section 6.1 binds the Company (our party, the customer) and restricts the products it may sell online, including an open-ended sweep to 'products substantially similar to Deerskin Products' and named third-party competitor lines — a field-of-use/non-compete deviation under NONCOMPETE. The reciprocal restriction on HDI in 6.3 is correctly left alone.

Redline reaches the playbook fallback: the vague 'any project similar to the Site … or products substantially similar' scope is replaced with a narrow, defined prohibition (operating a self-contained 'Deerskin'-branded consumer site), it remains term-only with no post-term tail, and express carve-outs for other channels, internal development and acquisitions are added — matching the fallback's required carve-outs and avoiding the walk-away triggers (undefined scope, post-term tail).

Edit is internally consistent and enforceable: the narrowed restriction mirrors HDI's retained 'Deerskin' brand exclusivity, and the carve-out paragraph expressly preserves the Company's right to source, build and sell substantially similar products through any other channel.

Failed 'minimal edit' check (0.779 changed-character ratio) is not disqualifying here: the original scope language is inherently open-ended, so narrowing to the fallback necessarily requires rewriting the operative restriction rather than a surgical deletion; the remainder of the sentence (HDI exclusivity) is preserved.

Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural, states the preferred position (deletion), explains the change, and offers the narrowed form as a compromise citing HDI's investment — consistent with tone requirements.
